name: Theta Cygni
description: A naked-eye star 18.3 parsecs away, 1.7 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the CHARA Array.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 185395: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.861 +/- 0.015 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 1.697 +/- 0.03

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 185395: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.342 +/- 0.011

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 185395: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6381 +/- 65

distance.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 185395: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 54.55 +/- 0.15 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 18 parsecs away whose disc the CHARA Array measured: 1.7 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 0.861 milliarcseconds, which gives 1.697 solar radii and 6,381 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 5 and 10, HD 185395: limb-darkened diameter, R, Teff
